summary.headline: Vardhman Q1 FY27 margins rose on spinning yarn-size gains and raw-material trading gains; fabric utilisation remains weak as US orders slipped.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 numbers improved in both percentage and absolute terms, driven mainly by the spinning business through better yarn sizes and a partial trading gain on raw material bought before the cotton price rise. The fabric business lagged: absolute volumes were roughly flat YoY and 3-4% below Q4 FY26, because US orders were lost after a missed sampling season tied to US tariffs. Management expects the spinning margin to moderate as cheap inventory runs out, but sees a 13-14% margin as a reasonable direction. Capex is mostly complete, with biomass boilers starting and the Dhar (PM MITRA) site dependent on land and power by around December 2026 and June 2027.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Utilisation full, margins good and demand strong; gains came from yarn-size mix and partial raw-material trading gains. Yarn export rose to about 110 million kg/month from 95-100 million kg, mostly from China (about 7-8% of production).

segments.name: Fabric (cotton and synthetic)
segments.commentary: Weak utilisation after losing US season orders; management says prices pass-through on yarn is only 60-70%, leaving 20-30% unrecovered. New synthetic fabric line has 15 lakh meters/month capacity at 15-20% utilisation, with two brand approvals and production starting in August 2026.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 7,000 shirts/day; plan to double to 4.5 million (units as stated) with peak revenue of about INR300 crore at full utilisation, targeted around Q1 FY28 (about one year from now). Mix is about 30% export and 70% domestic brands.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 to show the benefit of higher yarn prices realised in April-May 2026, given the 3-month export and 45-day domestic order cover.
Management expects spinning margins to moderate after Q2 as low-cost cotton inventory is consumed, but not to fall back to the 2-3 year trough.
Management sees sales visibility for at least 3-4 months, but margins depend on when old cotton runs out and new cotton is consumed.
Management views 13-14% as a reasonable margin direction, equal to about USD0.80-0.90 per kg of yarn conversion.
Biomass boiler at Baddi started last week; second boiler in Madhya Pradesh expected in about a month; power projects to complete in about 3 months.
Remaining capex of about INR800-900 crore to flow into FY28; most of the INR3,600 crore plan is complete or due within FY27.
Dhar site: land expected by December 2026; power not before June 2027; project implementation of 10-12 months once started.
capex_capacity: Open-end spinning project of about 55-60 tonnes/day started construction last week; expected in about 10 months.
Biomass boiler at Baddi started last week; second in Madhya Pradesh expected in about a month.
Synthetic fabric capacity at 15 lakh meters/month, utilisation 15-20%, target 70-80% within 6 months.
Garment capacity expansion from about 7,000 shirts/day to 4.5 million (stated), peak revenue about INR300 crore.
Dhar PM MITRA site: construction to start only once land and power are confirmed; not included in the announced INR3,600 crore capex.
demand_pricing: Cotton: management expects prices to firm as global supply falls 2-3% a year and demand rises, creating a 3-4% supply gap for 1-2 years; New York futures rose from about USD0.67-0.68 to about USD0.80/lb.
Indian cotton (CCI) rose from about INR55,000 to about INR64,000 per candy, now aligned with international prices; MSP up 6-7% implies cotton not below INR65,000-66,000 next season.
Yarn: China and Bangladesh take about 60% of Indian yarn exports; China accounts for about 30% of the export pool. Chinese reserve cotton sold at about USD1.15-1.16/lb.
Spinning capacity: 12-13 million spindles closed in India over three years; only about 0.7-0.8 million spindles of expansion announced this year.
Fabric pricing: customers want 20-45 day lead times; management says organised players gain share as brands prefer single-vendor sourcing.
Export share of garments about 30%; domestic brands about 70%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spinning order book and does the price rise show up in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Export orders cover about 90-95 days and domestic about 45-50 days historically, with the same cover today. Management confirmed the April-May price gains should show in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability after Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will moderate as cheap inventory runs out, though not to the 2-3 year trough; trading margins may not persist at market cotton prices unless yarn rises further.

qa_highlights.question: Garment expansion economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Doubling capacity to 4.5 million (stated) could reach about INR300 crore revenue at 100%, with full operations about one year away due to worker training; the aim is stand-alone viability.

qa_highlights.question: Dhar capex and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhar capex is not included in the INR3,600 crore plan. Construction starts only once land is given (expected December 2026) and power is assured (not before June 2027).

qa_highlights.question: Cotton yarn spread and where margins settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 spot spread was about USD0.90/kg. Management said historical range is USD0.85-1.00, with 13-14% margins reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: Will China keep buying Indian yarn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Chinese yarn imports to continue because of high Chinese cotton prices (over USD1 per lb) and Xinjiang-cotton risk, though this is not confirmed beyond current months.

risks_watch: Cotton supply: El Nino-related rain variation, Brazil area down about 5%, and possible quality issues; management will watch crop estimates for 2-4 weeks.
Fabric utilisation and US order recovery, which management expects to improve over the next 2-3 months.
Unrecovered yarn cost: only 60-70% of yarn price rises passed on to fabric customers.
Cotton import window: duty-free import window only for the next 2-3 months; decisions taken daily.
Dhar land and power timelines (December 2026 and June 2027) and the garment plant ramp-up (about one year).
summary.management_tone: ["Confident on spinning and industry-wide supply tightening, with forward-looking claims on margins and cotton prices qualified as 'our view' and 'future will tell'. More cautious on fabric, where recovery is described as expected but not yet visible. Evasive on inventory levels and specific revenue or margin figures, which were not disclosed on the call."]
